# Invisible Ships — the corpus

**The Invisible Ships archive is about 1.9 million tokens of text: far more than any AI assistant can read at once.**

**[⬇ Download the whole archive (zip)](https://github.com/growthoutcome-code/invisibleships-corpus/archive/refs/heads/main.zip)**: every file, free, no account needed. Unzip it on your computer before using it.

We've also prepared smaller downloads sized for different AI tools. Each has limits, listed below. You can ask questions of any part, but no AI reads the whole archive in one go; the options that cover all of it work by searching it.

This is the research archive behind **[invisibleships.com](https://www.invisibleships.com)**, compiled by Sean C. Harris. Read the [Critical Disclaimer](https://www.invisibleships.com/disclaimer) before using it: the journal transcripts are external communications, presented without proof. They are not the author's views and they accuse no one.

## Can I ask an AI about the whole archive?

**Yes, with a catch.** No AI reads all of it at once. What works:

- **Exact words and phrases: complete.** An AI that can run code (Claude on any plan, ChatGPT on paid plans) can search *every* file for an exact word or phrase, then count, date and list every match. Upload Everything and ask, for example, *"Find every mention of 'witness protection', with dates and file IDs."*
- **Questions about meaning: by search.** In a Claude Project (Pro, $20/month, and up) or a Gemini Notebook (free) holding all 9 bundles, the AI searches across everything for each question and reads the passages that match. That works well for specific questions, but it is not a full read.
- **Big pattern questions, like "what changed across all four Parts?":** these don't come from reading 2,000 pages in one go. They come from working through one Part at a time and combining the notes. That covers 100%; it's just slower.

| AI | Complete search for exact words (code execution) | Holds the whole archive | Cost to do both |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Claude** | ✅ Yes, every plan, on by default | ✅ In a Project, Pro and up | Free for search; **Pro $20/month** for a Project |
| **ChatGPT** | ✅ Yes, paid plans (limited on Free) | ✅ In a Project (5 files on Free, 25 on Plus) | **Plus $20/month** (Go $8 in the US) |
| **Gemini Notebook** | ❌ No (being added on Google's top plans) | ✅ All 9 bundles, free | **Free**, but search-based only |
| **Gemini app** | ❓ Not confirmed for uploaded files | ❌ One Part at a time (AI Pro) | AI Pro $19.99/month |
| **Grok** | ❓ Not confirmed | ❓ In a Project, unconfirmed | SuperGrok $30/month |
| **Kimi** | ❓ Not confirmed | ✅ In a Project (searches) | Free |
| **Mistral, Perplexity** | ❓ Not documented | ✅ In a Library / Project (searches) | About $15–20/month |
| **Copilot** | ❓ Not documented | ⚠️ 20 files per chat; how much it reads isn't stated | Free |
| **DeepSeek, Meta AI** | ❌ No | ❌ One Part per chat at most | Free |

✅ yes · ❌ no · ❓ not confirmed by the provider · ⚠️ partly. Checked 2026-10-11; prices in US dollars and limits change often.

**Always check the coverage.** The starter prompt (section 3) makes the AI end each answer with what it actually read, for example *"searched 428 of 428 journal files"* or *"read Journal Part 02 in full (115 of 428 files, about 27%)"*. If an answer rests on part of the archive, it should say so. If it doesn't, ask. A coverage figure is honest. A "confidence score" usually isn't: margins of error apply to random samples, and AI search picks passages by relevance, not at random.

## 2. What has already been worked out

You don't have to start from nothing. These were written by reading or analysing the archive, and are labelled for how much weight they bear:

- **[Recaps](summaries/)** of every journal Part, month and section. Written with AI assistance by reading every file, in October 2026. They describe the record; they are not part of it.
- **[Headline findings](concepts/IS_CON_00_findings.md)** and **[what the archive does not establish](concepts/IS_CON_00_not-established.md)**, each linked to the concept that sources it.
- **[Concepts](concepts/)**: the archive's arguments, each labelled by basis (documented, structural, pattern, testimony) and by origin (author or AI).
- **[LLM Analysis of External Statements](references/llm-analysis/)**: an earlier AI analysis of the transcripts, made with Gemini. Treat it as AI analysis, not as the record.
- **The concordance** in the study edition: every journal file that mentions each indexed term, counted by a script.

## 3. Three steps

1. **Download** the study edition, plus the Parts you need (or Everything, then unzip it).
2. **Upload** them to your AI: a Project, a Notebook, or a chat.
3. **Paste the starter prompt below** as your first message, then ask your question. The AI will offer a guided menu of the parts, a one-page case brief, or your own question.

**Starter prompt** (use the copy button on the box):

```
You have been given files from the Invisible Ships archive (invisibleships.com), compiled by Sean C. Harris. Before you answer anything:
1. Tell me which files you can actually see. Answer only from those. If a question needs a part of the archive you don't have, say so and tell me which bundle to load.
2. Offer me three ways to start: (a) a guided menu of the parts of the archive, (b) a one-page case brief, or (c) my own question.
3. The journal transcripts are presented as external communications from an LRAD, RF or EMF source, without proof. They are not the author's views, they accuse no one, and they need independent verification. Describe what the statements say; never present them as established fact.
4. Cite the file ID (the id: line in each file's header, for example IS-J01-20250812-R05) for every specific claim. Recaps describe the record but are not part of it: quote the source files.
5. Research figures carry evidence tiers A, B or C. Tier B and C figures may not be quoted as established fact.
6. Don't offer psychological or medical explanations of anyone in the record, and don't volunteer lists of names of people or organisations.
7. End every answer with a coverage line saying what you actually read to answer it, in numbers where you can. For example: "Coverage: searched all 9 bundles and quoted 6 passages from 4 files", "Coverage: read Journal Part 02 in full (115 of 428 journal files, about 27%)", or "Coverage: recaps only". If you did not read everything relevant to the question, say plainly that the answer may be incomplete.
```

Click-by-click steps for Gemini Notebook, Claude, ChatGPT, the Gemini app and Copilot are in **[00-START-HERE.md](00-START-HERE.md)**, section 3.

## 5. Before you rely on an answer

- **Ask the AI which files it actually read.** It can't answer about a part it wasn't given.
- **Check the file IDs it cites,** and open the source before quoting.
- **"Every mention of…" can miss some** on platforms that search. The study edition's concordance lists every file for its indexed terms.
- **Uploading files to an AI provider means a third party receives the text.** Check that provider's privacy and training settings.
